item.title: CORN BACK ABOVE $5 AS RAIN KEEPS COMBINES PARKED
item.description: Corn closed $5.00, up 4 and a quarter cents, clawing back the round number it lost Friday while El Nino rain keeps the Belt's combines sitting in the shed. Soybean oil ran 2.7% on the back of soymeal's firm tone, the two products pulling in the same direction for once. • Corn Reclaims The Round Number • Soy Complex Leads On Products • Cattle Soft, Feeders Give More Back Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-05

item.title: CORN CLOSES UNDER $5 WITH HARVEST STUCK IN THE RAIN
item.description: Corn settled Friday at $4.97, soybeans at $12.77, both down 20 to 40 cents on the week by the wire's own math. Record El Nino rain has stalled harvest across the Corn Belt at the exact moment farmers need combines rolling and bins filling. • Grains Grind Lower Into Harvest • Cattle Soft, Hogs Firm Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-04

item.title: CRUDE SPLITS FROM DIESEL AS HARVEST STALLS IN THE RAIN
item.description: WTI settled $91.26 Friday, down 1.5%, while Dated Brent physical barrels reportedly cleared $120 the same day as Hormuz tanker strikes (ongoing since the Iran war began) widen the crude-diesel split. That spread is why your diesel bill isn't following the crude headline down. Action: Diesel buyers: lock the next 30 days of on-farm fuel now; WTI at $91.26 says cheap, physical diesel markets say otherwise. • Crude Down, Diesel Up, Same Barrel • Harvest Stalls, Basis Stays Put Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-03

item.title: CRUDE DROPS 3.5% AS GRAINS GRIND HIGHER ON NO NEWS
item.description: Corn held $5.00 flat, beans ticked up to $12.77, and crude fell 3.5% to $89.37 on Gulf export flow that's actually working this time. That's the real story today: oil giving back the fear premium while grains just sit there, unbothered. Action: Crude under $89.37 and falling: lock any diesel needs now, this Gulf-flow story isn't done unwinding. • Crude Gives Back More Ground • Grains Sit On Their Hands • Cattle Firm, Cull Cows Don't Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-02

item.title: CORN RUNS 1.1% AHEAD OF STOCKS, CRUDE UP ON GULF FLOWS
item.description: Corn's up 5 cents to $5.04, Chicago wheat added 8 cents to $6.80, and crude ran 3.3% to $92.08, all three moving before Quarterly Stocks even prints at 11 CT. That's not reaction, that's positioning, and positioning ahead of a Stocks report is a bet, not a read. Action: Unpriced corn in the bin: a close above $5.09 says the Stocks positioning was real, price another 10% there. • Grains Run Ahead Of Stocks • Crude Runs On Gulf Flow Reports Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-10-01

item.title: GRAINS TICK HIGHER AHEAD OF STOCKS DATA AT 11 CT
item.description: Corn's up a quarter-cent shy of $5.25, beans up a nickel-plus to $13.03, and none of it means much with Quarterly Grain Stocks landing at 11 CT. Nobody's positioning hard into a report that could move old-crop supply pictures either way. Every bushel priced this morning got priced without knowing what USDA knows. Action: Nothing to do at $5.25 corn ahead of Grain Stocks; a settle above $5.29 on the data is the first reason to move. • Grains Wait On Stocks • Cattle Cycle Turns, Slowly • Crude Holds The Iran Bid Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-09-30

item.title: CRUDE PULLS BACK 2.1% AS YANBU REOPENS
item.description: WTI settled $92.12, down 2.1%, the first real give-back after two days running toward $96 on Iran-Hormuz fear. Saudi Arabia just restarted loadings at Yanbu on the Red Sea after the East-West pipeline came back partial, and that's a supply story beating a fear story today. Action: Diesel buyers: WTI at **$92.12** is the cheapest print in three sessions; lock the next fuel load now before any bounce back to $94. • Crude Gives Back The Fear Premium • Grains Drift On Empty China Wires Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-09-29

item.description: Crude added 2.1% to $93.19 and it isn't demand talking, it's one vessel crossing the Strait of Hormuz Wednesday, stuck below the 10-day average with the Iran-Hormuz cycle still refusing to fully unwind. item.title: GRAINS GIVE BACK THE CHINA POP AHEAD OF XI SUMMIT
item.description: Corn settled $5.29, down 3½ cents, wheat down a penny and three-quarters, both giving back Monday's China-hope pop before Thursday's Trump-Xi summit even opens. item.title: CORN RALLIES ON CHINA HOPES; CATTLE JUMP 2.4%
item.description: Corn ran 15 cents to three-week highs and beans gained 24 cents overnight on fresh hope for a US-China trade deal, but both gave it back into the close, corn settling $5.38 and beans $13.19, both down on the day. item.title: BEANS SANK FRIDAY; SUMMIT WEEK OPENS WITH CROSSED SIGNALS
item.description: Soybeans closed Friday at $13.03, down 16 cents on the week's last session as funds took profits ahead of the Trump-Xi summit set for Sep 24. item.title: CRUDE BREAKS 5.6%; BEANS WAIT FOR XI
item.description: Saudi Aramco's Gulf reroute -- started this week after the East-West pipeline shifted 60 million barrels back through the Persian Gulf -- knocked crude down 5.6% to **$95.47**, its biggest single-session drop in months. Relief, not shortage, is what the market priced Friday. Diesel harvest risk hasn't left; it just got cheaper to ignore. Action: Unpriced new-crop beans: hold through the weekend. item.title: SEPTEMBER WASDE PRINTS; BEANS GIVE BACK 24 CENTS
item.description: The September WASDE printed Thursday, and Friday the market said what it thought: soybeans at $12.99 gave back 24 cents, the sharpest single-session drop in weeks, while December corn at $5.32 actually added a nickel. The USDA printed something, the funds sold beans and held corn, and now the question is whether $12.99 is the new floor or the first step lower. Friday's WASDE report sent soybeans lower and corn sideways, while crude fell hard on the Saudi pipeline story reversing course. • WASDE PRINTS; BEANS FOLD → If you have unpriced new-crop beans, $12.99 is the line. A close below $12.85 next week says the WASDE break has legs; price on that signal, not ahead of it. • CRUDE FALLS ON SAUDI PIPELINE REVERSAL • CATTLE FIRMS; HOGS SLIP Read more: https://agsist.com/daily/2026-09-12

item.title: WASDE AT 11 CT; CRUDE DROPS 4%, BEANS FIRM
item.description: Soybeans firmed to $13.17 at the 52-week high while crude fell hard to $99.06, its sharpest one-session drop in weeks, as the whole complex repositioned ahead of the September WASDE at 11 CT. The meal/bean side held; the energy side gave back two weeks of war premium in one morning. WASDE decides which part of the market read this week correctly. item.title: BRENT HITS $100; GRAINS AND CATTLE FOLLOW
item.description: WTI settled at **$95.26**, its highest close in two months, after the US destroyed five Iranian tankers and Iran struck US forces in Jordan, the sharpest re-escalation of the Iran-Hormuz cycle since its July flare. item.title: WHEAT BREAKS 3.4%; SEPTEMBER WASDE COUNTDOWN BEGINS
item.description: Wheat closed $7.16, down 3.4% Friday, the biggest single-session drop in the complex. Corn drifted to $5.12 on light volume as Labor Day weekend stripped the room. Beans held better at $12.94, off just 1.1%. The whole week telegraphs one thing: the funds took profits before the holiday and are waiting for Thursday's export sales and Friday's WASDE to decide their next move. Friday's pre-holiday profit-taking hit wheat hardest while corn and beans drifted; the September 11 WASDE is the week's make-or-break event. • WHEAT BREAKS; GRAINS DRIFT • CATTLE QUIET; TRUMP ORDERS MOVE • ENERGY AND INPUTS INTO HARVEST → If you have unpriced fall diesel needs, the EIA crack-spread data says the current rack price is not the top of the range. item.title: WHEAT DROPS 3.4%; DIESEL TIGHTENS INTO HARVEST
item.description: Wheat closed Friday at $7.16, down 3.4%, the sharpest single-session drop in this complex in weeks. Diesel crack spreads widened to record levels according to EIA data, meaning the fuel bill for first-pass harvest is higher than any budget penciled in last spring. The September 11 WASDE is six days out and the market is walking in with a bearish lean on wheat and a diesel problem. Friday's close put wheat at its worst session in weeks while diesel crack spreads widened, squeezing fall fieldwork budgets before the September 11 WASDE. • WHEAT BREAKS; GRAINS DRIFT • CATTLE QUIET; POLICY NOISE RISES • DIESEL TIGHTENS; CRUDE HOLDS → If you haven't locked fall diesel at current rack prices, the EIA data says waiting is not working in your favor.
